quests.instruction: FLICK THE COIN TO VERIFY THE FACT
quests.passage: [Abyss Vent 1-1] Water near hydrothermal vents can reach temperatures of 350 degrees Celsius, which is high enough to melt lead. However, the extreme hydrostatic pressure at the bottom of the ocean prevents the water from boiling.
quests.question: The water near deep-sea hydrothermal vents remains liquid due to the extreme pressure, despite being hot enough to melt lead.
quests.hint: Check the last sentence discussing boiling and pressure conditions. (Diving calibration index 1-1)
quests.explanation: At great oceanic depths, immense pressure raises the water's boiling point, allowing it to reach superheated states while remaining liquid. [Validated by Fact Check Unit 1].

quests.instruction: FLICK THE COIN TO VERIFY THE FACT
quests.passage: [Coral Zone 1-2] Although coral reefs cover less than 0.1% of the world's ocean surface, they host and nurture over 25% of all marine life, earning them the nickname 'rainforests of the sea'.
quests.question: Coral reefs occupy more than 10% of the Earth's total ocean surface area.
quests.hint: Review the exact percentage of ocean surface area covered by reefs in the first sentence. (Diving calibration index 1-2)
quests.explanation: Coral reefs cover a tiny fraction (less than 0.1%) of the ocean surface, but concentrate an immense proportion of biodiversity. [Validated by Fact Check Unit 1].

quests.instruction: FLICK THE COIN TO VERIFY THE FACT
quests.passage: [Biolum Lab 1-3] Bioluminescence is cold light produced chemically by deep-sea organisms. Unlike artificial lightbulbs, this biological light generates zero heat, allowing creatures to conserve vital energy.
quests.question: Bioluminescence produces a significant amount of heat energy alongside light.
quests.hint: Compare biological light emission to artificial light sources described in the text. (Diving calibration index 1-3)
quests.explanation: Bioluminescent light is known as 'cold light' because nearly 100% of the energy is emitted as light, generating no heat. [Validated by Fact Check Unit 1].

quests.instruction: FLICK THE COIN TO VERIFY THE FACT
quests.passage: [Whale Pod 2-1] Blue whales are filter feeders that consume up to four tons of tiny krill every day. They do not possess teeth; instead, they have baleen plates that act as a giant sieve to trap food.

quests.hint: Find the anatomical description of how blue whales filter their food. (Diving calibration index 2-1)
quests.explanation: Blue whales are toothless baleen whales; they filter massive swarms of tiny krill through fiber-like baleen plates. [Validated by Fact Check Unit 2].

quests.instruction: FLICK THE COIN TO VERIFY THE FACT
quests.passage: [Wave Pulse 2-2] In the open ocean, tsunami waves travel at speeds exceeding 800 kilometers per hour. As they approach shallow coastal waters, they slow down significantly but grow taller.

quests.hint: Look at the second sentence outlining speed and wave height shifts near coasts. (Diving calibration index 2-2)
quests.explanation: Tsunamis slow down due to friction in shallow waters, causing the energy to compress and build tall, destructive wave heights. [Validated by Fact Check Unit 2].

quests.instruction: FLICK THE COIN TO VERIFY THE FACT
quests.passage: [Vent Hub 2-3] Undersea hydrothermal vent ecosystems are unique because they do not rely on sunlight. Instead, specialized bacteria perform chemosynthesis to convert toxic vent hydrogen sulfide into energy.

quests.passage: [Kelp Forest 3-1] Giant kelp grows in cool, nutrient-dense ocean waters. Under optimal conditions, these massive marine algae can grow at an astonishing rate of up to 60 centimeters per day.
